4_doctor_s_best_magnesiu.name: 4 Doctor's Best Magnesium
4_doctor_s_best_magnesiu.notes:
Doctor's Best Magnesium Glycinate, 4 tablets (800 mg magnesium total). Multiple reasons:

• Sleep quality — glycinate contains glycine, an inhibitory neurotransmitter that promotes calm.
• Cramps and recovery — heavy lifting + sweating + a deficit all increase magnesium demand; calf cramps are often magnesium-adjacent.
• Cardiovascular — mild blood pressure lowering, modest insulin sensitivity.
• Constipation prevention — lower food intake + high protein slows transit.

Glycinate specifically because it's highly bioavailable AND non-laxative, unlike oxide (poorly absorbed) or citrate (loose stools at higher doses). Dinner timing keeps it away from caffeine (which antagonizes magnesium) and lets the calming effect help sleep.

braunschweiger_john_morrell.notes: John Morrell Braunschweiger (pork liver sausage), 16oz/454g package, 8 servings of 2 oz (56g). Label per 56g: 170 kcal (Fat Cal 110), 13g fat (4.5g sat, 0 trans), 115mg cholesterol (38% DV), 480mg sodium (20%), 5g total carb, 0g fiber, <1g sugars, 8g protein, Vitamin A 150%, Vitamin C 0%, Calcium 0%, Iron 45%. NOTE: this is an OLD-FORMAT panel (pre-2016 -- 'Fat Cal.', Vitamin A/C listed, no added-sugars line), so %DV values use the old Daily Values: Vit A 150% of 5000 IU = ~2250mcg RAE/serving; Iron 45% of 18mg = ~8.1mg/serving. kcal NEEDS NO CORRECTION: 8x4 + 13x9 + 5x4 = 169 vs label 170. Essentially exact. SUGAR sub-threshold: label reads '<1g'; estimated 0.5g/serving with ~0.4g added (corn syrup, dextrose, and sugar all appear in the ingredient list). PROTEIN IS LOW FOR A MEAT (8g per 170 kcal = 21 kcal per gram of protein) -- this is a fat-dominant emulsified sausage, not a lean protein source; fat supplies ~65% of calories. LIVER-DRIVEN MICRONUTRIENTS, from USDA FDC 171621 (braunschweiger, pork) per 100g: vitamin B12 20.09mcg (837% DV), vitamin A 4220mcg RAE (469%), riboflavin 1.5mg (117%), selenium 58mcg (105%), pantothenic acid 3.4mg (68%), niacin 8.4mg, iron 11mg, copper 0.24mg, zinc 2.8mg, phosphorus 168mg, potassium 199mg, folate 44mcg, choline ~250mg. VITAMIN A NOTE: ~2250mcg RAE per serving is PREFORMED retinol (not beta-carotene). The tolerable upper intake level for preformed vitamin A in adults is 3000mcg/day, so a single 2 oz serving supplies about 75% of that ceiling. Unlike carotenoids, preformed retinol accumulates and has a defined upper limit -- worth knowing if liver is eaten regularly. Factual note, not a recommendation. PURINES ~1.8 mg/g => ~100mg per 56g serving -- HIGH. Organ meats/liver are the single highest-purine food category and the classic gout trigger. Relevant to uric-acid tracking. MEDIUM confidence (liver ~290mg/100g; this product is part liver, part pork/bacon). CURED product: contains sodium nitrite plus sodium erythorbate (cure accelerator), potassium lactate and sodium diacetate (antimicrobials), and SODIUM PHOSPHATES (from the bacon component) -- additive phosphate, absorbed more completely than the liver's intrinsic phosphorus. Ingredients: pork liver, pork, bacon (pork, water, salt, sugar, sodium phosphates, sodium erythorbate, sodium nitrite), water, modified food starch, and 2% or less of corn syrup, salt, flavorings, potassium lactate, sodium lactate, dehydrated onion, sodium diacetate, dextrose, sodium erythorbate, sugar, sodium nitrite. cheese_provolone_lucerne.name: Cheese provolone slices not smoked (Lucerne)
cheese_provolone_lucerne.notes: Lucerne Dairy Farms NOT SMOKED Provolone Cheese Slices, 12 slices, net wt 8 oz (226 g). Label serving 1 slice (19 g); 12 x 19 = 228 g vs 226 g declared net, so slices average ~18.8 g. LABEL-EXACT per 19 g slice (high confidence): 70 kcal, 5 g fat (3 g sat, 0 trans), 15 mg cholesterol, 135 mg sodium, 0 g total carb, 0 g fiber, 0 g sugars, 5 g protein, vit D 0.1 mcg, calcium 140 mg, iron 0.1 mg, potassium 30 mg. CARB SUB-THRESHOLD CORRECTION: label shows 0 g total carb and 0 g sugars, meaning <0.5 g per slice. Not left at zero. USDA carbohydrate-by-difference for provolone is 2.14 g/100 g, but by-difference (100 minus water+protein+fat+ash) absorbs all analytical error and overstates residual carbohydrate in an aged cheese where lactose is largely fermented out. Used USDA's DIRECTLY MEASURED total sugars instead: 0.57 g/100 g = 0.0057 g/g = ~0.11 g per slice. Carbs set equal to sugars. MEDIUM confidence. CALORIE RECONCILIATION: Atwater on the declared macros gives 5x9 + 5x4 + 0.11x4 = 45 + 20 + 0.4 = 65.4 kcal, and generic USDA provolone scales to 351 x 0.19 = 66.7 kcal per 19 g -- both BELOW the label's 70. The label therefore runs ~5-7% HIGH, not low; the manufacturer likely computed from unrounded values nearer 5.4 g fat / 5.1 g protein, which is within normal batch variation for a fattier provolone. NO CORRECTION APPLIED -- kept at the label's 70 kcal. Correcting downward would mean logging fewer calories than the manufacturer declares, which is the wrong direction of error for a deficit. OFF-LABEL MICROS estimated from USDA SR Legacy 170850 (Cheese, provolone), per-100 g values divided by 100 (MEDIUM-HIGH confidence -- the Lucerne label and USDA agree closely on the anchors they share: sodium 710 vs 737 mg/100 g, calcium 737 vs 767, protein 26.3 vs 26.1 g, fat 26.3 vs 27.1 g): phosphorus 503 mg/100 g (~96 mg/slice), magnesium 28.6, zinc 3.29, selenium 14.6 mcg, copper 0.036 mg, vit A 239 mcg RAE, vit E 0.25 mg, vit K 2.2 mcg, B1 0.036, B2 0.32, B3 0.14, B5 0.50, B6 0.071 mg, B9 10 mcg, B12 1.46 mcg, choline 15.7 mg, water 41.4%. IODINE ~30 mcg/100 g -- LOW confidence, not in USDA for this food; estimated from the dairy-iodine range and set consistent with the American-slice entry in this catalog. PURINES ~6 mg/100 g -- LOW, cheese is a gout-favorable protein source. Whole-milk natural cheese, NOT a processed 'cheese product': ingredients are provolone cheese (cultured pasteurized milk, salt, microbial enzymes) only -- no emulsifying salts, no added phosphate, no anticaking agent. Microbial rennet, so vegetarian. rBST-free pledge. Protein is complete dairy casein, no quality downgrade. Use within 3-5 days of opening. CONTAINS milk.

instructions: Crack 4 eggs into a wide microwave-safe bowl. Whisk with 1/8 tsp salt and 1 tsp olive oil (oil keeps the eggs from going rubbery). Drop in 150 g frozen pre-cooked shrimp and 100 g frozen shelled edamame. Spread everything out in a single layer.

First-time cook is data collection — adjust ±30 sec next time based on how it came out. Magic Chef HMM1611ST, 1100W output. Shrimp and edamame must both be the pre-cooked frozen kind.

eggs_shrimp_skillet.name: Eggs & shrimp microwave bowl
instructions: Crack 4 eggs into a wide microwave-safe bowl. Whisk with 1/8 tsp salt (or skip salt entirely — soy sauce + shrimp's processing salt is plenty), ~1 tsp soy sauce, and 1 tsp olive oil. Drop in 100 g frozen pre-cooked shrimp and spread them out.

Old-format label (Calories from Fat, Sugars, Vitamin A/C %). Serving 2 slices (56 g), 8 servings per container => 16 slices, ~28 g each. Iron converted at the OLD 18 mg RDI: 2% = 0.36 mg per 56 g. Label states it is not a significant source of dietary fiber, vitamin C or calcium -- fiber set to 0, calcium taken from USDA. CALORIE RECONCILIATION (+3 kcal correction applied, 60 -> 63 per 56 g): (1) Strict Atwater on the DECLARED macros gives 2x9 + 2x4 + 10x4 = 18 + 8 + 40 = 66 kcal, 10% above label. (2) But 'Calories from Fat 15' pins unrounded fat at 15/9 = 1.67 g, not 2.0 -- so fat contributes 15, not 18. (3) The 2 g total carb is not all sugar: label sugars are 1 g, and the cure contains POTASSIUM LACTATE, whose lactate counts in carbohydrate-by-difference at ~3.6 kcal/g rather than 4. So 1 g sugar x 4 = 4.0 plus ~1 g lactate x 3.6 = 3.6, total 7.6 kcal from carb. (4) Rebuild: 15.3 (fat, 1.7 g) + 40.0 (protein, 10 g) + 7.6 (carb) = 62.9 => 63 kcal per 56 g = 1.125 kcal/g. FAT STORED AT THE UNROUNDED 1.7 g, not the declared 2 g, so the item is internally consistent with that kcal. CONFIDENCE LOW-MEDIUM on the correction: USDA's independent profile for this exact food class scales to 60.9 kcal per 56 g, which supports the label's 60 outright, and the gap is entirely attributable to this product carrying ~1.6 g more carb per serving than the USDA sample. Keeping 60 would also be defensible; 63 is the middle course and errs upward. ADDED SUGAR: all 1 g of sugars is from the cure (sugar is an ingredient; ham contributes no native sugar), so addedSugar = total sugars. OFF-LABEL MICROS from USDA SR Legacy 173863 / SR 07028, 'Ham, sliced, pre-packaged, deli meat (96% fat free, water added)' -- an exact class match, and it agrees closely with the label on shared anchors (kcal 108.7 vs 107.1 per 100 g, protein 17.0 vs 17.9 g, sodium 945 vs 1018 mg). MEDIUM-HIGH confidence: magnesium 19.1 mg/100 g, phosphorus 252 (stored slightly higher at 260 for the added sodium phosphates), zinc 1.52, calcium 5.2, copper 0.043 mg, selenium 31.7 mcg, iodine 1.22 mcg, B1 0.348, B2 0.261, B3 5.65, B5 0.696, B6 0.391 mg, B9 0, B12 0.348 mcg, choline 62.6 mg, vit D 0.61 mcg, vit E 0.30 mg, vit K 0.43 mcg (as MK-4), water 74.8%. Pork is an excellent thiamine (B1) source -- one serving carries roughly 16% DV despite only 63 kcal. POTASSIUM stored at 500 mg/100 g vs USDA's 463 -- raised because POTASSIUM LACTATE is an explicit cure ingredient here and the USDA sample may not carry it. LOW-MEDIUM confidence, plausible range 460-600. PURINES ~120 mg/100 g -- moderate, and lower per gram than solid ham because the product is brine-extended to ~75% water. LOW-MEDIUM confidence. SODIUM IS THE HEADLINE NUMBER: 570 mg per 56 g serving = 1018 mg/100 g, 24% DV for two slices. Among the most sodium-dense items in this catalog on a per-calorie basis (16 mg sodium per kcal). Ingredients: cured with water, contains 2% or less of salt, sugar, potassium lactate, sodium phosphates, sodium diacetate, sodium erythorbate (antioxidant, limits nitrosamine formation), sodium nitrite (preservative). LOW-FAT DIET PLAN (current 1400 kcal cut, half avocado/day = ~11-15g fat):
- Half avocado covers 1-2 softgels at full absorption.
- Default: 2 softgels with the avocado meal, 1 softgel with whichever other meal has the most incidental fat (eggs, dairy, salmon, chicken thigh; even 3-5 g of fat helps a lot vs dry).
- If no other meal has any fat: drop to 1-2 softgels that day. 1,440 mg well-absorbed beats 2,160 mg with the 3rd barely getting in.
- Salmon days: dietary EPA+DHA from salmon (~1-1.5 g per 100 g Atlantic) covers a chunk of the daily target; 1-2 softgels is fine.
- Stacking all 3 with avocado works too if you drizzle a teaspoon of olive oil to push the meal past the 15 g fat threshold (and accept the fish-burps).

SPLITTING ACROSS MEALS (when fat is available at each):
- Each dose gets its own micelle pool = better absorption per dose.
- Eliminates the fish-burps / reflux that 3-at-once tends to cause.
- Steady tissue EPA/DHA saturation across the day.

EMERGENCY RULE (skipped meal, dry softgel imminent): take it with even a small fat-bearing bite (teaspoon olive oil, slice of cheese, glass of milk, handful of nuts). Or delay to the next meal that has fat. Dry softgel = ~one-third absorbed.

water_recipe.name: Water (recipe ingredient)
water_recipe.notes: Plain water, for use as a RECIPE INGREDIENT. Purpose is to account for MASS in composed recipes so that per-gram values compute correctly when water is part of a mixture (a smoothie, a sauce, reconstituted powder). Contributes zero calories and zero macronutrients. 1 mL = 1 g exactly, so gram and millilitre amounts are interchangeable here. SEPARATE from the existing 'water' item in this catalog, which is deliberately configured for HYDRATION SCHEDULING -- its display units are wake / pre-lunch / afternoon / dinner at 500 mL each with daily times attached, and it sits in the 'water' category. That one is left untouched. This entry is filed under 'liquids' instead of 'water' so that using it inside recipes does not get double-counted into daily hydration totals. MINERALS DELIBERATELY LEFT AT ZERO rather than estimated. Tap water genuinely does contain calcium, magnesium, sodium, and fluoride, but the amounts vary by more than an order of magnitude between municipalities (calcium roughly 5-100 mg/L, magnesium 1-30 mg/L, sodium 5-50 mg/L), and filtered, softened, distilled, and bottled water differ again. Inventing a number would be worse than recording none. If a local water-quality report is ever available the fields can be filled in properly. COOKING CAVEAT: water that BOILS OFF does not remain in the finished dish. When building a recipe that simmers, reduces, or bakes, count only the water that stays in the final product -- otherwise the recipe's total mass is overstated and its per-gram calorie density comes out too low. For pasta or grains the reverse applies: they ABSORB water and gain mass, which is why cooked-weight values differ from dry.
